We have a Linux mini-PC (the gateway) in our home office that needs to reach several productivity tools running exclusively on our MacBook on the same local network. The MacBook sometimes goes to sleep, so we need a recovery mechanism for that too.

The gateway already has a configuration file at `/workspace/home/node/.openclaw/openclaw.json` that describes which tools are active, which Mac hosts own them, and the MacBook's Wake-on-LAN details.

Please go through the full setup workflow:
1. First, discover and print the current ownership map based on the existing config.
2. Install the appropriate bridge wrappers into the gateway's tool directory, making sure the installation auto-selects only the tools that are actually enabled in the config — do not manually list them. Wire up the Wake-on-LAN recovery using the details already in the config. Since the enabled tools are spread across two different Mac hosts, you will need to provide a fallback default host as well (pick any reasonable `user@host` value).
3. Finally, run a verification pass that respects the enabled/disabled status from the config rather than blindly checking every possible tool.

All relevant scripts are already available under `/workspace/scripts/`.
